title: Canada will match US tariffs 'dollar for dollar' as trade talks break down
titleZh: Canada will match US tariffs 'dollar for dollar' as trade talks break down
author: tartoran
relevanceReason: 命中 1 个 AI/科技关键词。
summaryRaw: 1 day agoNadine Yousif,Senior Canada reporterandToby MannReutersPrime Minister Mark Carney said progress in the talks was not enough to meet Canada's objectivesA fresh wave of US tariffs on a wide array of Canadian goods came into effect on Saturday after a last-minute breakdown in trade talks.Announcing the suspension of negotiations shortly before the Friday night deadline, Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney said he would impose reciprocal tariffs on US goods "dollar for dollar".Carney said "last-minute changes in the US proposed terms were unfair, uneconomic, and called into question the reliability of any deal".Trade negotiators had been engaged in intense talks since July, after President Donald Trump threatened to impose a 50% levy on nearly $20bn (C$28bn; £14bn) of Canadian imports by 19 August.Trump had temporarily paused those tariffs earlier in the week, saying the two sides were close to signing a trade deal that was "very good" for both countries.But minutes before the deadline for a deal, Carney said that while "important progress" had been made in the talks it was "not enough to meet our objectives for Canadians"."As a result, this evening, I have decided to suspend trade negotiations with the US and have directed negotiators to return to Ottawa," he said."Last-minute changes in the US proposed terms were unfair, uneconomic, and called into question the reliability of any deal."After Carney's announcement US trade representative Jamieson Greer said in a statement: "Tonight, Canada declined to finalise the trade deal under the terms agreed earlier this week."Despite the US offer to Canada to receive the best treatment of any major exporter to our market, new demands and walk backs of other commitments by Canada have upended the careful balance reached in the past days."The breakdown in talks marks a significant shift in tone from earlier in the week, when both US and Canadian officials sounded optimistic that a trade deal beneficial for both countries was within reach. Negotiators were reportedly discussing a deal that would reduce US tariffs on Canadian steel and aluminium from 50% to 25%, and on Canadian autos from 25% to 15%.In exchange, Carney had asked Canadian provinces to restore US alcohol to store shelves. The breakdown of the talks puts the US-Canada relationship in uncharted territory, and will be a major test for Carney's premiership. The two countries have developed one of the world's most deeply economically integrated trading relationships, and Canada sends approximately 70% of its exports south.But tensions between the two major trading partners have been simmering since Trump returned to office in January last year and unleashed a wide-ranging global programme of tariffs, upending decades of free trade between Canada and the US.Now that talks have broken down, Canada will be hit with new 50% US tariffs imposed by Trump using a Depression-era law called the Tariff Act of 1930. They will be applied on a range of goods, about 5% of Canadian exports, including wine, dairy, cement, clothing and hockey equipment.The new levies are in addition to existing tariffs the US had already imposed on Canadian steel and aluminium, autos and lumber.Businesses and stakeholders on both sides of the border had pushed for a deal to be reached, arguing that the new US tariffs on Canada will be harmful to both countries.In a statement, the Canadian Chamber of Commerce called the tariffs "a body blow to North American competitiveness"."For a small Canadian exporter operating on tight margins, this isn't an abstract trade dispute. It means looking at your orders, your payroll and your employees and asking what you can still afford," said the chamber's president Candace Laing.Canadians have told pollsters that they are willing to fight for a good deal. A recent survey by firm Abacus Data suggested that around 36% of Canadians would support retaliating to US tariffs, while another 30% would want the Carney government to continue negotiating.The prime minister will need to convince Canadians that the economic pain is worth the cost of standing up to the White House is search of a better agreement in the long run.Financial analysts have projected the new 50% tariffs could reduce the country's GDP by 0.3% to 0.6%.Doug Ford, premier of Canada's most populous province Ontario, said "the prime minister has my full support for a strong response - tariff for tariff, dollar for dollar".Ontario, which has a large manufacturing and auto sector, has been among the hardest hit of Canada's provinces in this trade dispute. The economies of Quebec and British Columbia are also going to be especially exposed to the new tariffs. British Columbia Premier David Eby said in a statement on Friday night that "our politeness should never be mistaken for weakness"."We didn't ask for this, but we'll keep fighting for as long as it takes."Canada has been engaged in on-again, off-again trade negotiations with the US for over a year in pursuit of a deal that would see the US drop or reduce tariffs on these key sectors. The US, meanwhile, has been asking for a number of concessions from Canada, including removing its remaining retaliatory tariffs on American autos and adjusting its dairy quotas to allow greater access for US cheese producers.It has also asked that the ban on US alcohol sales, imposed last year by most Canadian provinces in retaliation to Trump's tariffs, be removed.In a statement on Saturday, the Distilled Spirits Council of the United States said it was "unfortunate that the Canadian provinces' continued refusal to return US spirits products to store shelves has led to this outcome". It said exports to Canada fell more than 70% year-over-year from the start of the retaliatory ban in March through December 2025.

comments.author: hunglee2
comments.textRawHtml:
The world should've collectively recognised what Liberation Day was and responded together, in lock step, and in kind.

Instead, the Europeans caved, Japanese caved (PM resigned after doing so), Republic of Korea caved (PM resigned after doing so), India of course caved and so on, shattering any prospect of collective action which might pull the rogue hegemon back into line.

Now, the US is simply able to renege or renegotiate the bilateral deals whenever he feels like it, forcing the other party to face down the US by themselves - not many can do this, maybe only China. Anyways, I wish the Canadians well and I hope they gain global support
comments.textZhHtml:
世界应该集体认识到什么是解放日，并共同做出反应，步调一致，以同样的方式做出反应。

相反，欧洲屈服了，日本屈服了（首相辞职后辞职），韩国屈服了（总理辞职后当然辞职了），印度屈服了等等，粉碎了任何可能将流氓霸权拉回正轨的集体行动的前景。

现在，美国只要他愿意，他就能随时食言或重新谈判双边协议，迫使对方自己面对美国——没有多少人能做到这一点，也许只有中国。不管怎样，我祝愿加拿大人一切顺利，并希望他们获得全球的支持

children.author: LeFantome
children.textRawHtml:
You are both right. The world capitulates more than it should. But the world is also moving away and building contingencies.

The world needs leadership. And Canada is helping with that.

I do not think that reciprocal tariffs are actually the answer though. They hurt both sides and the US is not a rational enough actor to respond like you hope they will. The answer is in shifting trade away from the US and isolating their economy. It takes longer but it is what will work. And even if their behaviour does not change, their power will fade with their economy.
children.textZhHtml:
你们都是对的。世界的屈服超出了应有的程度。但世界也在逐渐远离并引发突发事件。

世界需要领导力。加拿大正在为此提供帮助。

但我认为互惠关税实际上并不是答案。他们伤害了双方，而美国不是一个足够理性的行为体，无法像你希望的那样做出回应。答案是将贸易从美国转移并孤立其经济。这需要更长的时间，但这是有效的。即使他们的行为不改变，他们的权力也会随着经济的发展而减弱。

children.author: swat535
children.textRawHtml:
As a Canadian, my hope is that we can build stronger relations with Europe. I don't think anyone can avoid China but I would rather minimize those ties.

We can't afford to cut all ties with United States due to our geography and history, however it would be prudent for us to reduce our dependency.

I don't think majority of Canadians wish to see the nation in such a vulnerable position again with regards to US. Banking on a single player in terms of security and trade has proven to be a risky endeavor.

I have much love for the American people, but I support the actions of our government.

children.author: YZF
children.textRawHtml:
As a fellow Canadian. Our neighbor is the world's biggest economy. Despite their current "challenges" they are still very close to us in values and culture. Our paths are interlocked. We are not going to decouple from the USA and it's not in our interest to do so.

When a Canadian new grad is faced with an option of going to work in SV or in China which do they prefer? Between Chinese values and American values which do we prefer? A society with no freedom of speech? Where people are arbitrarily jailed if they voice an opinion against the government? Where the government places citizens in concentration and re-education camps and runs them over with tanks? I mean to me the choice is clear.

How many large American companies have offices in Canada? How many people and what slice of the economy does this support? Lots.

So yes, the US has drifted and is drifting from the ideal. And maybe it was never the ideal. But it's much closer to us than China in every imaginable facet and will likely remain so for the next many decades. We need to filter the noise out, definitely stand firmly for what we believe in, but also compromise and look at the longer term.

children.author: maxglute
children.textRawHtml:
>some benign benevolent power

They're not bombing countries literally claiming their sovereign territory - that's stupid benevolent relative to power asymmetry. PRC inherited all territorial disputes and resolved ~12/14 land border disputes, most with more concessions. In SCS, which is multi party, they're the only ones who made any concession (11 dash to 9 dash), and offered resource sharing in lieu intractable resolution. Meaning PRC not only did not create any border disputes, but proactively resolved most peacefully and tries to resolve current peacefully. There's a reason most remaining disputes are from democracies where ceding or even splitting is political suicide. And frankly party in territorial disputes who thinks they should get 100 vs PRC should get 0 (basically what losers in wars gets) is retarded and in the wrong... and frankly that is the level of delulu PRC is peacefully dealing with.

That makes PRC like most benevolent rising power in recorded history. There's no fallacy, one measure powers behavior relative to other comparable powers - and relative to all historic powers - PRC is objectively benevolent.

children.author: YZF
children.textRawHtml:
China could change but it is a totalitarian regime with no human rights and a terrible track record. I would be happy to see a change there towards freedom, democracy and human rights but that doesn't seem to be in the cards.

I don't have a quantitative way of measuring this but I disagree Europe and Canada are closer in values. Canada has some "Europe" in it but a lot more "North America". If you put a random American and a random Canadian in one room they'll have a lot more common than a random Canadian and a random European. Random examples are suburbia and gun ownership.

Many Canadians are dual-citizens. About a million US citizens live in Canada. Many Canadians work and travel to the US. Business, personal, family relationships etc. Similarly about a million Canadians live in the US.

I've worked a lot with Europeans and Americans (I still do, I work for a large American company with offices in both). I've traveled to the US and to Europe. If you've done that a lot then you know the difference in feeling and culture.

children.textRawHtml:
I think this is a fair take, but also the US does this because it can. I don't think other countries don't do imperialism because they are morally pure, but because to do so means getting into conflict with the US. The US just has the biggest stick and so can push around other nations with impunity.

The US domestically has a commendable historic commitment to free expression and press freedom, which are good things that China does badly. Those things deserve to be commended even while we condemn imperialism. China has its own record of imperialism in Nepal and its ambitions to attack Taiwan. It just doesn't (currently) have the position to act with impunity the US has long enjoyed.
